decision.summary: The washing machine repair on 28/02 failed after a few washes and the tenant reported it again on 04/03. The old job NBL-042 was closed, so I opened linked ticket JOB-101 and asked Lantern Services to revisit. The tenant and landlord have been told.

answers.question: Where does this case stand and what is outstanding?
answers.answer: NBL-042 was closed on 28/02 after Lantern Services replaced the heating element wiring (£75 + VAT). The fault returned within about 5 days. A revisit is outstanding. Lantern's invoice is also on file, but its due date of 22 July 2026 looks wrong.

answers.question: What is the next action, who is it for, and through which channel?
answers.answer: Done: I opened JOB-101 linked to NBL-042. I emailed Lantern Services to arrange the revisit and find the cause of the failure. I emailed the tenant with a routine 14-day target, and emailed the landlord an update. No visit date is booked yet because Lantern will agree it with the tenant.

answers.question: Does anything need a human decision?
answers.answer: Not now. A human decision is needed only if Lantern quotes further work or a replacement above the spend limit. A human may also want to check whether the first repair was fit for purpose before the invoice is paid, and to check the odd invoice due date.

actions_claimed.description: Emailed tenant with update and timescale

conflicts: NBL-042 was not found in the ticket system, and the list of tickets was empty, so I relied on the case history.
The appointment slot of 23/02 3.25pm conflicts with the call that agreed Tuesday 1pm.
The Lantern invoice due date of July 2026 looks anomalous.
The event 021 hold said we were waiting on the invoice, but the job was later closed with no photos or quote.
assumptions: Lantern Services remains the right contractor for a rework visit.
The landlord's earlier approval covered the engineer visit only, so any new spend needs fresh approval.
The tenant's own description of the fault is accurate.
